key_insight: CareConnect shows that a tightly scoped, safety-first LLM agent can automate healthcare scheduling and logistics reliably without providing medical advice.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce administrative burden and improve access to care by speeding up booking, rescheduling, cancellation, and facility information retrieval.
method: Built a conversational agent with LLM function calling, retrieval-augmented generation, and deterministic safety guardrails.
Orchestrated eight domain-specific tools for appointment and facility workflows.
Used emergency detection and medical-intent refusal to short-circuit unsafe requests.
evidence_signal: In 680 benchmark scenarios, the system achieved 91.8% task completion, 96.0% safety compliance on safety-critical cases, 2.2-second median latency, and $0.0324 average cost per appointment.
watch_item: Performance depends on strict scope control and robust integration with legacy scheduling systems, so deployment may require careful validation and monitoring.
paper_title: Toward Trustworthy Large Language Model Agents in Healthcare
